chunks: What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who died while only women were present with him. He said: A woman who is his mahram should perform his ghusl, and the women should pour water over him, and his garment should not be removed. And if it is a woman who died among men, while there is no woman with her and no mahram for her, then she should be buried as she is in her clothes. But if a mahram of hers is with her, he should wash her from over her clothes. The second view is that this may be understood to mean that they wash her by pouring water over her, just as we mentioned regarding their washing of the man, because that has indeed been narrated. And if all of that is understood as being recommended, then the basic principle is what we stated earlier: the obligation of burying her without ghusl.

key_terms.تُغَسِّلُهُ: she performs the ritual washing of the deceased body
key_terms.ثَوْبُهُ: his garment, which remains on the body during the washing in this case
key_terms.ذَاتُ مَحْرَمٍ: a woman who has a legally unmarriageable kinship relation to him
key_terms.غُسْلٍ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a close relative with whom marriage is forbidden and who affects legal rulings of bodily handling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man or woman dies while only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for washing the deceased when only members of the opposite sex are present, with special consideration for mahram relations and preservation of covering. It indicates that a deceased man may be washed by a mahram woman without removing his clothes, while a deceased woman without a female attendant or mahram may be buried in her clothes without ghusl, though an alternate transmitted view mentions pouring water over her from above her garments.
